chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Therefore avoid the uncleanness of the idols and avoid the false words.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The singing (music).'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic phrase 'avoid the false words' refer to according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this concise hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a specific exegetical interpretation (tafsir) of Quran 22:30, equating 'false words' (qawl al-zur) with 'singing' (al-ghina'). This establishes a direct theological link between the Quranic command to avoid idolatrous impurities and the prohibition of musical singing, a view central to Shia jurisprudence regarding the permissibility of music.
